segments.english:
12269—Umm Ma'qal al-Asadiyya:[7]

[1] al-Thiqat 3/461; A'lam al-Nisa 5/63; al-Tajrid 2/335; Usd al-Ghaba, entry (7607); al-Isti'ab, entry (3675).

[2] Ahmad transmitted it in Musnad Ahmad 2/526, from Abu Hurayra.

[3] Usd al-Ghaba, entry (7608).

[4] In manuscript A: “and he separated her from the Khuza'i woman.”

[5] Omitted from manuscript A.

[6] Umm Mu'attib.

[7] A'lam al-Nisa 5/64; al-Tajrid 2/336; Taqrib al-Tahdhib 2/625; Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 12/480; al-Kashif 3/392; Tahdhib al-Kamal 3/1706; al-Istibsar 358; Khulasat Tadhhib 3/403; Talqih Fuhum Ahl al-Athar 370; Usd al-Ghaba, entry (7609); al-Isti'ab, entry (3678).

segments.arabic:
زوج أبي معقل، ويقال: إنها أشجعية. ويقال أنصارية.
روى حديثها أصحاب السنن الثلاثة.
وقد تقدم بيان ذلك مفصلا في ترجمة زوجها في كنى الرجال، وذكر الاختلاف في سند حديثها:
«عمرة في رمضان تعدل حجّة» .
ويقال: إنها المرادة بما وقع
في حديث ابن عباس في الصحيح- أن النبي ﵌ قال لامرأة من الأنصار: «ما منعك أن تحجّي معنا»؟ قالت: كان لنا ناضح فركبه أبو فلان وابنة لزوجها وابنها. قال: «فإذا كان من رمضان اعتمري، فإن عمرة في رمضان تعدل حجّة» «١» .
ولكن ثبت في مسلم أنها أم سنان، فإما أن يكون اختلف في كنيتها، وإما أن تكون القصة تعددت، وهو الأشبه.
segments.english:
The wife of Abu Ma'qil. It is also said that she was of Ashja', and it is said that she was an Ansari woman.

The authors of the three Sunan collections transmitted her hadith.

A detailed explanation of this has already appeared in the biography of her husband among the men's kunyas, together with mention of the disagreement concerning the chain of transmission of her hadith:

“An 'umra in Ramadan is equivalent to a pilgrimage.”

It is also said that she is the woman intended in the report of Ibn 'Abbas in the Sahih: the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said to a woman of the Ansar, “What prevented you from performing the pilgrimage with us?” She replied, “We had a water-carrying camel, which Abu So-and-so and his son—her husband and her son—rode.” He said, “When Ramadan comes, perform an 'umra, for an 'umra in Ramadan is equivalent to a pilgrimage.” (1)

It is established in Muslim, however, that she was Umm Sinan. Thus, either there was disagreement over her kunya, or the incident occurred more than once; the latter is more likely.

unresolved.explanation: The note unambiguously reads “Umm Mu'attib,” which has been preserved. The supplied witnesses do not establish whether it represents a variant heading, a correction, or a separate cross-reference.
